Sec. 8. Monitoring and Assessing of the Students’ Status

8.1. Monitoring. To assure that the enrolment or status of the student is correct and aligned, the student who is primarily held responsible for his/her status of enrolment may make use of the following records:

8.1.1. Copy of Grades (COG). The copy of the grade is issued at the end of the semester by the Office of the Registrar to the student where the grades for the course/subjects taken are indicated.

8.1.1.1. Any concern on the student's standing is indicated in the COG, such as INC for completion and/or enrollment status such as warning, probation, dismissal, or disqualification.

8.1.1.2. COG is used by the Dean of the College for the evaluation of the student during enrolment for updating of records.

8.1.2. LSPU Portal. The student may also access his/her academic records or standing by logging into his/her account in the LSPU Portal (myaccount.lspu.edu.ph).

Article 2. Definition of Terms

1.1. Industry refers to companies involved in services and production of goods for sale especially in a factory.

1.2. Internship refers to a period of time spent receiving or completing training at a job both to apply classroom learning and to be exposed to professional workplace.

1.3. Host Training Establishment (HTE) refers to agencies, institutions, or establishments whom the University has partnered with and entrusted the students for work immersion and learning experience.

1.4. Internship Manual refers to the document detailing the policies and guidelines for the conduct of the internship/on-the-job training of the students.

1.5. Internship Plan refers to the curriculum and competency outline detailing what the student should be able to attain in the course of the internship/on-the-job training program as prepared and approved by the University and the HTE.

1.6. Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) refers to the document that records the details of an agreement between the University and the HTE, detailing the objectives, plan, scope, expectations and activities among other composites of the agreement.

trace.answer_for_eval:
A COR (Certificate of Registration) is a document certifying that a student is officially enrolled for a semester, required for admission to classes, and signed by authorized university officials. It can be viewed online via the student portal or claimed as a printed copy from the Registrar.

A COG (Copy of Grades) is an official record of a student's grades for a semester issued by the Registrar, indicating grades for courses taken and enrollment status flags such as Warning, Probation, Dismissal, Disqualification, or INC. It is used for retention evaluation and academic standing monitoring.

The main difference is that the COR certifies enrollment status, while the COG provides academic performance and standing information.
